analyst_view.overall: Galatasaray are 18th of 36 with 6 points and Aston Villa 6th with 9, so both have plenty at stake: Okan Buruk's side want to climb into the top 24 at home, Villa want a top-8 place. Galatasaray are flying at home, top of the Süper Lig after five straight wins, but their attack is short: Victor Osimhen (knee arthroscopy, top scorer with 9 league goals) is listed out by two previews and at best a bench option per one NTV Spor report, Roland Sallai (back-muscle strain) and Ismail Jakobs (groin) are out, and Rafael Leão is in rehab in Doha. What changed: the numbers now count only Leão, not Osimhen, Sallai or Jakobs, so I now trim Galatasaray's attack myself instead of leaving it to the numbers. Villa drew 0-0 with Sunderland on Saturday; Matty Cash (concussion), Matteo Ruggeri and Amadou Onana are counted, Victor Lindelöf is ill and doubtful. No referee is named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals (1.3 Galatasaray, 1.7 Villa) and take off only Leão (-5% on Galatasaray's goals) plus Cash for Villa. Osimhen, Galatasaray's top scorer, is very likely out or only on the bench after knee surgery, and Sallai is out too; Jakobs missing at left-back helps Villa a little, but overall I trim to about 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners, already counting Galatasaray's slight rise in corners won (+2.8%) and Villa's dip (-3.3%). Villa had long spells of possession against Sunderland and will push wide, while Galatasaray lose width without Leão and Sallai; these pull in opposite directions, so I stay at 8.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards, with Galatasaray's quieter recent card count (-8.5%) and Villa's slight rise (+3.6%) already in. RAMS Park is loud and hostile, but that is part of the home record the numbers use, and no referee is named yet, so I stay at 3.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.6 shots (12.8 Galatasaray, 13.7 Villa) and do not take the missing forwards off Galatasaray's shots. Without Osimhen and Sallai, young Deniz Gül is expected to lead the line, so Galatasaray lose their main shot-taker; I trim to about 25.5, a little more than yesterday because the numbers no longer count Osimhen at all.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 shots on target, already counting Villa's sharper recent finishing (+6.0%) and Galatasaray's slight dip (-0.9%). Osimhen is the forward who turns chances into shots on target, and he is very likely out or only a late option, so I lean lower, to about 9.7.
